mobilisation of calcium from bone into blood.

 $$ \therefore $$ t = $$\sqrt {{{2hm} \over {qE}}} $$

proton.


Since, electron has smaller mass so it will take
smaller time.

$$\overrightarrow v  = {v_0}\widehat i$$ (v<sub>0</sub> > 0)
 enters an electric field
$$\overrightarrow E  =  - {\overrightarrow E _0}\widehat i$$
 (E<sub>0</sub>
 = constant > 0) at t = 0. If $$\lambda $$<sub>0</sub>
is its de-Broglie wavelength initially, then its
de- Broglie wavelength at time t is
questions.explanation:
Given, Initial velocity v = v<sub>0</sub> $$\widehat i$$


Electric field E = – E<sub>0</sub>$$\widehat i$$


$$ \therefore $$Initial de-Brogile wavelength,


$$\lambda $$<sub>0</sub> = $${h \over {m{v_0}}}$$


Now force due to electric field on electrons,


$$\overrightarrow F  = \left( { - e} \right)\left( { - {E_0}\widehat i} \right) = e{E_0}\widehat i$$


Acceleration produced in the electron,


$$\overrightarrow a  = {{\overrightarrow F } \over m} = {{e{E_0}} \over m}\widehat i$$


Now, velocity of electron after time t,


$$\overrightarrow {{v_t}}  = \overrightarrow v  + \overrightarrow a t$$ = $$\left( {{v_0} + {{e{E_0}t} \over m}} \right)\widehat i$$


$$ \Rightarrow $$ $$\left| {\overrightarrow {{v_t}} } \right| = {v_0} + {{e{E_0}t} \over m}$$


Now, $$\lambda $$<sub>t</sub> = $${h \over {m{v_t}}}$$


= $${h \over {m\left( {{v_0} + {{e{E_0}t} \over m}} \right)}}$$


= $${h \over {m{v_0}\left( {1 + {{e{E_0}t} \over {m{v_0}}}} \right)}}$$


= $${{{\lambda _0}} \over {\left( {1 + {{e{E_0}t} \over {m{v_0}}}} \right)}}$$ [As $${\lambda _0} = {h \over {m{v_0}}}$$]

 (where $${\upsilon _0}$$
 is
threshold frequency), is incident on a metal
plate, the maximum velocity of electrons
emitted is v<sub>1</sub>
. When the frequency of the
incident radiation is increased to 5$${\upsilon _0}$$
, the
maximum velocity of electrons emitted from
the same plate is v<sub>2</sub>
. The ratio of v<sub>1</sub>
 to v<sub>2</sub>
 is
questions.explanation:
From Einstein’s equation


$${1 \over 2}mv_1^2 = 2h{\nu _0} - h{\nu _0} = h{\nu _0}$$


Again, $${1 \over 2}mv_2^2 = 5h{\nu _0} - h{\nu _0} = 4h{\nu _0}$$


$$ \therefore $$ $${{{v_1}} \over {{v_2}}} = \sqrt {{1 \over 4}}  = {1 \over 2}$$

due to heating
